outcome: A matched benchmark decides whether async-first execution becomes the supported Core profile or the synchronous baseline remains current.
currentProblem: Implementation of async scheduling is not evidence of product value. ExHarness needs a held-out matched comparison that measures quality-adjusted cost, turn reduction, cache behavior, steering and recovery before changing the supported execution profile.
constraints: Baseline and candidate use exact same model/version, task inputs, tool budget, source and acceptance semantics.
Accepted quality cannot be traded away silently for token savings; the non-inferiority bound and cost gate are fixed before results.
All attempts, failures, retries and human interventions are reported; selected successful runs cannot decide promotion.
Promotion changes only a versioned HOW/execution profile; it does not alter product acceptance or external-effect authority.
successCriteria: Held-out matched runs report accepted quality, total/provider input-output-cached tokens, cost, model turns, tool calls, useful operations per turn, overlap, elapsed time and recovery outcomes.
The candidate passes a predeclared quality non-regression bound and cost/token improvement gate or the decision is KEEP_SYNC_BASELINE.
No duplicate external effects, lost terminal results, unsafe cancellation or recovery regressions occur in negative probes.
